fundamentals.name: Datadog, Inc.
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Datadog, Inc. operates an observability and security platform for cloud applications in the United States and internationally. The company's products comprise infrastructure and application performance monitoring, log management, observability pipelines, synthetics, real user monitoring, product analytics, continuous profiler, database monitoring, data observability, LLM observability, error tracking, network monitoring, incident response, workflow automation and App builder, event management, bits AI SRE, cloud cost management, cloud security, code security, cloud SIEM, threat management, sensitive data scanner, and CI visibility. Datadog, Inc. was incorporated in 2010 and is headquartered in New York, New York.

judgment.summary: Rapidly growing software company with strong revenue and earnings growth, but high valuation and thin operating margins.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter beat EPS estimates by 18.3%; next earnings date is 2026-08-06.
positives: Revenue growth 32.2% YoY and quarterly earnings growth 113.4% indicate strong top and bottom-line expansion.
Gross margin of 79.9% is very healthy, suggesting efficient service delivery.
Free cash flow of $936.73M indicates strong cash generation capabilities.
Analyst consensus is 'strong_buy' with a mean target of $225.34, suggesting upside potential.
Current ratio of 3.40 and quick ratio of 3.29 show excellent short-term liquidity.
negatives: Trailing P/E of 587.36 and Forward P/E of 80.49 indicate a very high valuation.
Operating margin of 0.8% and profit margin of 3.7% are thin, despite high gross margins.
Return on assets of -0.2% is negative, indicating inefficient asset utilization.
Debt/Equity ratio of 32.22 is high, though offset by strong cash reserves and liquidity.

news.paragraph: Datadog (DDOG) has seen a flurry of positive analyst attention, with B of A Securities raising its price target to $280 and maintaining a buy rating. The company was also highlighted as a top performer in May and is increasingly viewed as a critical player in the software sector. These developments suggest strong underlying business momentum, even as the stock trades at a premium valuation.
